item.title: Six Flags to reopen Goliath rollercoaster – but now with seatbelts after recent rider death
item.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
item.content:encoded: Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem fell from ride earlier this month, spurring amusement park to temporarily shut it downSix Flags will install seatbelts on its Goliath rollercoaster in Georgia, after a rider plummeted to his death earlier this month.Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, a 42-year-old father and educator, was thrown from his seat on the Goliath, a coaster that plunges riders down 165ft, before a second drop of 180ft. On his way down, he collided with the ride’s other cars.Continue reading...

item.title: Hundreds of thousands march in France as protests take place across Europe – Europe live
item.author: Patrick Daly(now);Marina Dunbar , Frances Mao and Emily Mackay (earlier)
item.content:encoded: French police have made 1,000 arrests and Italian officers have raided homes in Milan, with protests also taking place in Spain and AlbaniaJesse, 40, a charity worker from the north of Paris, had turned out for the street march.She said: “I’m so angry. I’m here to support schoolchildren’s demands for better conditions. I’m so proud of them and we have to stand together.”Continue reading...

item.title: Tens of thousands of Lula supporters rally on eve of Brazilian election runoff
item.author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro and Tiago Rogero in Belo Horizonte
item.content:encoded: Nearly 159 million people to head to polls on Sunday in battle between leftwing incumbent and Flávio BolsonaroTens of thousands of supporters of Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, have streamed on to Rio’s most famous beach for a giant protest they hope will propel him towards a historic election fightback against his far-right rival, Flávio Bolsonaro.Nearly 159m Brazilians will vote in the election’s runoff on Sunday, with the pair tied in the polls after Bolsonaro won the first round on 4 October by 47% to 45%.Continue reading...

item.title: Manhunt under way to find prisoner who absconded from medical facility
item.author: Patrick Daly and Press Association
item.content:encoded: Met police say Anthony Lloyd, 38, was last seen on Friday in south London, and ‘poses a risk to himself and the public’A manhunt is under way to locate a prisoner who police say “poses a risk both to himself and the public” after he absconded from a medical facility in London.Anthony Lloyd forced his way out of a health unit in Lewisham, in south-east London, shortly after 4pm on Friday, the Metropolitan police said.Continue reading...

item.title: She Planned to Protest Trump. She Didn’t Plan on Getting Punched.
item.author: Jessica Contrera
item.content:encoded: Blake Miley yelled “fascist” as President Trump spoke at a midterm campaign rally. The violence that followed “was not right,” she said.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands march across France in protests over schools and policing
item.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
item.content:encoded: Government estimates at least 400,000 people took part, but trade unions say the number is double thatHundreds of thousands marched in cities across France on Saturday in largely peaceful protests to support schoolchildren’s demands for more teachers and repairs to dilapidated buildings, as Emmanuel Macron faces a social and political crisis in his final months as president.In Paris, at least 110,000 people marched along the eastern edge of the city, according to government estimates. They supported high schoolers but also complained of the high cost of living and the government’s heavy policing, saying riot police had been sent to target school protesters over the past month, instead of the government offering political solutions.Continue reading...

item.title: Netanyahu Is Up for Re-election After Years of War. How Will Voters See Him?
item.author: Isabel Kershner
item.content:encoded: The Oct. 7 attacks marred Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s image as Mr. Security. Ahead of elections, he’s trying to sell Israelis on the new, hawkish version of himself.

item.title: Ukraine’s military says Starlink satellite connection stable after recent restrictions
item.author: Donna Ferguson
item.content:encoded: Volodymyr Zelenskyy offers thanks to US allies for restoring system key to air defence and ‘frontline logistics’Ukraine’s military has a “stable connection to Starlink”, the Ukrainian government has said, 10 days after its ability to use the satellite communications system was suddenly restricted.The Starlink satellite terminals, which are produced by Elon Musk’s SpaceX but managed by the US government, are a key component of Ukraine’s military operations. Sudden speed restrictions on the terminals, which capped operations at speeds of 160km/h (99mph), led to the failure of several Ukrainian combat missions earlier this month.Continue reading...

item.title: Sam Fender tells fans high ticket prices for Proper Massive tour are ‘getting changed’
item.author: Priya Bharadia
item.content:encoded: Fender criticises stadium pricing, calling it ‘bollocks’ and says it ‘won’t be happening’ on his tourSam Fender has responded to criticism by fans about ticket prices for his 2027 stadium tour by promising he would lower the cost, telling followers on Instagram: “They’re getting changed.”The 32-year-old musician announced his Proper Massive stadium tour earlier this week.Continue reading...

item.title: Northern Olympics campaign to get £7m in Healey’s budget
item.author: Sammy Gecsoyler
item.content:encoded: Fund will support feasibility study for potential bid to host Games in 2040s, backed by northern mayors and top athletesJohn Healey is to announce a £7m fund to examine a potential future bid to host the Olympics in northern England in his first budget as chancellor.The fund will be used to carry out a full feasibility study for a northern Games, which, if successful, would be held in the north of England in the 2040s.Continue reading...

item.title: Israel Cracks Down in West Bank City After Deadly Attack
item.author: Aaron Boxerman and Fatima AbdulKarim
item.content:encoded: Hundreds of Palestinian families fled their homes as the Israeli military raided Hebron. The operation came a day after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers.

item.title: Suspect arrested over fire at Hitler’s ‘Eagle’s Nest’ retreat in Bavaria
item.author: Donna Ferguson and agencies
item.content:encoded: About 200 firefighters deployed to tackle blaze at former Nazi mountain retreat in remote part of southern GermanyPolice have arrested a 33-year-old German citizen after a fire ripped through Adolf Hitler’s former mountain retreat in Bavaria, leaving the historic Nazi meeting place – known as the Eagle’s Nest – largely destroyed.About 200 firefighters were deployed on Friday night to tackle the blaze at the Nazi dictator’s remote, purpose-built Kehlsteinhaus residence, a protected building on the peak of Obersalzberg in southern Germany.Continue reading...

item.title: Nine killed and 40 injured after gunmen open fire at church funeral in Jordan
item.author: Reuters in Al-Mushairfeh
item.content:encoded: Footage broadcast on state TV shows three attackers approaching Greek Orthodox church and firing shotsNine people have been killed after gunmen opened fire at a funeral at a church in Jordan in a rare attack ⁠on the country’s Christian minority.Authorities described the attack on Friday as a terrorist act by extremists.Continue reading...

item.title: Met says it shared allegations about Meghan’s father with her but not other forces
item.author: Harry Taylor
item.content:encoded: Scotland Yard says it shared letter about Thomas Markle Sr allegations in 2019 but did not pass claims to other agenciesThe Metropolitan police have confirmed they gave a letter to the Duchess of Sussex in 2019 concerning “alleged offending” involving her father, after accusations arose on Friday about Thomas Markle Sr having child sexual abuse images.Scotland Yard said it had received a letter in January 2019 making a number of allegations about offending outside Britain.Continue reading...

item.title: Kim Jong-un crosses newly opened bridge into China
item.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
item.content:encoded: North Korean leader travels over New Yalu River Bridge to meet senior Communist party memberKim Jong-un has visited China, inaugurating a bridge that connects the two countries and saying he hopes to expand cooperation with his neighbour.The North Korean leader arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday after crossing the New Yalu River Bridge, according to South Korea’s unification ministry, which handles affairs related to North Korea, and China’s official Xinhua news agency.Continue reading...

item.title: Storm Boelo to bring 80mph gusts and heavy rain to parts of UK
item.author: Priya Bharadia
item.content:encoded: Second named storm will hit northern parts of UK as thousands remain without power after Friday’s Storm AustenThe UK is bracing for a second storm this weekend, as strong winds and heavy rain are expected to disrupt travel and cause further power cuts in the north.Storm Boelo, the second named storm of the season, is expected to bring heavy, frequent showers and winds potentially exceeding 80mph to northern parts of the UK.Continue reading...

item.title: Israeli soldiers raze neighbourhood in Hebron, driving families from homes
item.author: Julian Borger in Jerusalem
item.content:encoded: PM Benjamin Netanyahu vows ‘to destroy this place’ in retaliation for militant attack on army checkpointIsraeli troops have levelled a neighbourhood in Hebron, driving out hundreds of families in collective punishment for a militant attack on an army checkpoint outside the West Bank city, local Palestinian authorities said.The Hebron municipality estimated that 35 hectares (86 acres) had been destroyed or marked for destruction and about 1,500 people had been evicted from their homes by Saturday afternoon in the district of Ein Deir Baha. The whole city of 250,000 people was sealed off by checkpoints on every point of entry.Continue reading...

item.author: Eric Lipton, Maxine Joselow and Mira Rojanasakul
item.content:encoded: The president temporarily waived clean-air rules for industrial facilities that spew cancer-causing gases. Then his appointees worked to gut the regulations altogether.

item.title: Additional 178 cases of measles reported by US health authorities amid outbreak
item.author: Jessica Glenza
item.content:encoded: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 4,588 cases across the country, more than double the tally in 2025Federal health authorities reported an additional 178 cases of measles in the US this week, as the vaccine-preventable illness continues to sicken people across at least 43 outbreaks.The new data reported by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) comes as experts criticize the agency for lack of transparency, and as health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr takes steps to further upend US vaccine infrastructure.Continue reading...

item.title: Epstein files take back seat in midterms but experts say issue has not gone away
item.author: Victoria Bekiempis
item.content:encoded: Other voter concerns have prevailed but return of Congress likely to see renewed focus on late sex offender’s activitiesAs US voters head to the polls for crucial and fraught midterm elections, some survivors’ advocates in the Jeffrey Epstein investigation have expressed concern that the scandal could recede into the background.Political experts believe, however, the Epstein issue is not going away permanently and that many voters can balance day-to-day concerns such as affordability and AI with the scandal involving the late financier and accused sex trafficker whose social circle was widespread among America’s elite.Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: Hope, dread and the final stretch to Election Day.

item.title: ICC prosecutor says court making ‘significant progress’ despite US sanctions
item.author: Julian Borger Senior international correspondent
item.content:encoded: Nazhat Shameem Khan claims some staff are facing ‘banking difficulties’ but their work is unaffectedThe deputy prosecutor of the international criminal court has said new US sanctions are beginning to take effect on its staff but insisted they have not hindered the court’s work.The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, announced the sanctions this month, accusing the ICC – a frequent target of the Trump administration – of being a “rogue court” and declaring: “Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC.”Continue reading...

item.title: New Trump rule allows hunters to bait bears in Alaska with doughnuts, bacon and more
item.author: Tom Perkins
item.content:encoded: Critics decry Trump administration rule that lets hunters lure bears with human foods on federal lands in AlaskaA new Trump administration rule allows hunters to bait bears on federal lands in Alaska with bacon, doughnuts, meat scraps or other human foods typically used to help kill the trophy animals at close range.Opponents say the practice will cause bears to be more aggressive around humans, and allege that the rule change is a political gift to largely rightwing trophy hunters. The rule replaces a 2024 Biden administration rule that banned the practice, and environmental groups criticized the move as “indefensible and inexcusable”.Continue reading...

item.title: No unions, low taxes: why some of Britain’s top chefs are opening outposts in Gulf states
item.author: Helena Horton
item.content:encoded: Leading restaurateur says Gulf countries actively help businesses set up, while east Asia has a better work ethicSome of London’s top restaurants are opening branches in Dubai because of a “tax tsunami” in the UK and better work ethic abroad, according to a leading restaurateur.James Robson, a co-owner of Fallow in St James’s Market, regarded as the capital’s hottest restaurant, serving 1,000 people a day, has just signed a deal to open an outpost in the Gulf.Continue reading...

item.author: Harry Taylor

item.title: Dónal Lunny, ‘colossus of Irish music’, dies aged 79
item.author: Press Association
item.content:encoded: Founding member of Planxty, Lunny went on to play for bands such as Moving Hearts, the Bothy Band and CoolfinThe Irish traditional musician Dónal Lunny has died at the age of 79 from cancer.Lunny rose to prominence in the trio Rakes of Kildare alongside his brother Frank and Christy Moore. He went on to play in bands such as Planxty, Moving Hearts, the Bothy Band and Coolfin among others and toured the world.Continue reading...

item.title: As a divided Israel prepares to go to the polls, can Netanyahu pull off his greatest political trick yet?
item.author: Jonathan Freedland in Modi’in
item.content:encoded: The prime minister has defined and dominated his country’s politics for three decades and is putting his rivals on the defensive before Tuesday’s general electionThey chant his name, they cheer and clap – and yet he is not the most dominant person in the room. Looming over the crowd that has gathered to hear Gadi Eisenkot, the former general who is the lead opposition challenger in Tuesday’s Israeli election, is a man who is not there. It is the man Eisenkot seeks to replace as prime minister, the man who first served in that role three decades ago and who has held it, on and off, for 19 of the past 30 years. It is Benjamin Netanyahu.Naturally, the warm-up speakers at this evening rally in the modest city of Modi’in, halfway between Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, stress the virtues of Eisenkot, a son of working-class Moroccan Jews who rose through the ranks to become chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces and entered politics only four years ago. But every sentence might as well end with two words that go unspoken: .Continue reading...

item.title: Typhoon Champi kills one and injures more than 500 in Taiwan as it heads to China
item.author: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Super typhoon weakening but large parts of Taiwan, including Taipei, still mostly closed and flights cancelledTyphoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday killing one person, injuring more than 500, and uprooting trees and severing power as it weakened and ⁠headed north toward ⁠the ​Chinese coast.Earlier classified as a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the ⁠Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of about 126km per hour (78 miles per hour) near its ⁠centre, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA).Continue reading...

item.title: Embattled Greens senator Jordon Steele-John confirms leave from parliament after allegations against him made public
item.author: Sarah Basford Canales
item.content:encoded: WA politician says he considered attending Senate estimates virtually but was told it would be ‘unacceptable’Jordon Steele-John has confirmed he will not attend parliament next week as the embattled Greens senator apologises for publicly releasing the letter outlining the claims against him.On Saturday afternoon, Steele-John removed a social media post containing a three-page letter marked as “confidential” sent to the Greens leader, David Shoebridge, earlier this month. The letter urged an investigation into allegations he had acted inappropriately towards women between 2017 and 2025.Continue reading...

item.title: Helen Haines’s condition improves days after losing both legs from alleged attack
item.author: Adeshola Ore
item.content:encoded: Independent MP now serious but stable, according to update from Melbourne’s Alfred hospitalIndependent MP Helen Haines’s condition has been downgraded to serious but stable after she lost both legs following an alleged attack near her electorate office in north-east Victoria on Monday afternoon.The Alfred hospital in Melbourne provided an update on Haines’s condition on Saturday morning.Continue reading...

item.title: Rubio tells Cubans ‘now is the time’ to act to see political change
item.author: Guardian staff and agencies
item.content:encoded: US secretary of state makes comments after Trump tells US rally warships could intervene on return from IranMarco Rubio urged Cubans seeking political change in their country to act, saying “now is the time” moments after Donald Trump told a Friday rally for candidates in south Florida that US warships could intervene in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war.The US secretary of state, in his social media post addressed “to those who seek to create positive change”, urged Cubans to capitalize on Trump’s plans. “The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete [sic] partnership with the CIA,” Rubio said.Continue reading...

item.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and flash flooding predicted for much of Australia
item.author: Adeshola Ore with Australian Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Parts of Queensland, Victoria and South Australia can expect severe storms on Saturday, moving into NSW and Tasmania by SundaySevere thunderstorms and heavy rain will sweep across most Australian states this weekend, adding to the deluge in an already drenched Queensland.Flash flooding in south-east Queensland this week prompted hundreds of SES callouts and the closure of multiple schools. On Saturday morning, the Bureau of Meteorology had nine flood warnings in place for south Queensland.Continue reading...

item.title: Why Legal Experts See the Justice Dept.’s Alaska Election Challenge as Dubious
item.author: Charlie Savage
item.content:encoded: No obvious legal authority supports a pre-emptive effort to block the certification of Alaska’s Senate election if the Republican incumbent narrowly loses.

item.title: Jordon Steele-John’s position remains in limbo as Greens prepare for moment in spotlight
item.author: Sarah Basford Canales
item.content:encoded: David Shoebridge’s newly-minted leadership under pressure over handling of misconduct allegations as Senate estimates loomsMore than a week after allegations that Greens senator Jordon Steele-John had behaved inappropriately towards women made headlines, his position in the party remains in limbo and its new leader’s handling of the issue in question.Continue reading...

item.title: Israel launches collective punishment campaign in Hebron after two soldiers killed
item.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem and Lorenzo Tondo
item.content:encoded: Benjamin Netanyahu and ministers promise demolitions and forced displacement after deadly gunfightIsrael has launched a campaign of collective punishment against Palestinians in Hebron after gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers and injured three near a checkpoint outside the city.Benjamin Netanyahu announced a siege on Hebron and neighbouring Halhul and said residents of the gunmen’s home neighbourhoods would all be forced out. He promised mass demolitions of homes.Continue reading...

item.title: Duchess of Sussex ‘deeply distressed’ over child sexual abuse image claims against father
item.author: Caroline Davies
item.content:encoded: Meghan reveals she was made aware of ‘disturbing allegations’ against him in 2018 by Met policeThe Duchess of Sussex has said she is “deeply distressed” over accusations involving child sexual abuse images against her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr, and revealed she was made aware of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018 by the Metropolitan police.Meghan issued a statement after the Sun newspaper published claims that her half-brother Thomas Markle Jr alleged he had found a stash of images belonging to their father at his former home in the Philippines.Continue reading...

item.title: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
item.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
item.content:encoded: Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in UgandaHealth officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.Continue reading...

item.title: Magnitude-7 earthquake hits Tibet, killing at least 16 and destroying hundreds of homes
item.author: Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Search and rescue efforts under way after quake strikes region’s north, with at least seven aftershocks recordedA magnitude-7 earthquake has hit Tibet, killing at least 16 people, injuring 54 and destroying hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media have said.Search and rescue efforts continued after at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds collapsed, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. It was the biggest quake in the region in the past five years, according to China’s national broadcaster CCTV.Continue reading...

item.title: India slashes cost of cancer drugs after court rules mark-ups are ‘extortion’
item.author: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi
item.content:encoded: Case filed in 2022 by patient unable to afford medicine leads to cap on drug prices for millions who face ruin if diagnosedThe Indian government has moved to reduce the price of cancer drugs after a retired bank clerk took her case to the supreme court.From next month, 137 cancer drugs in India will be cheaper as the government tries to tackle the tragedy of poorer patients either forgoing treatment, selling land or falling into debt to meet the high cost of some medicines, which are making large profits for hospitals and pharmacists.Continue reading...

item.title: Jim Chalmers faces a world of hard choices where the solution to one problem makes the other worse
item.author: Patrick Commins
item.content:encoded: High inflation, low growth and rising unemployment can be added to the federal treasurer’s wall of worriesJim Chalmers in a speech last week offered the scant encouragement that the economy would be “a bit better” in a year’s time.Fast forward to Friday morning, and the treasurer revealed that his officials were busy downgrading their forecasts ahead of December’s mid-year budget update to show slower growth and higher unemployment.Continue reading...

item.title: Brazil’s election and the battle for the Amazon – podcast
item.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Tom Phillips; produced by Ivor Manley, Eli Block and Ross Burns; executive producer Sami Kent
item.content:encoded: Our Latin America correspondent, heads to Roraima to hear what’s at stake for the rainforest and the communities that live there in the Brazilian presidential runoff on Sunday. Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.comFor the Amazon and the communities who live there, the stakes in Sunday’s Brazilian presidential election runoff could scarcely be higher.Our Latin America correspondent, heads to Roraima, the country’s most northern state, to hear from voters, preachers and politicians in a region that heavily backed Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round.Continue reading...

item.title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix
item.author: Giles Richards in Austin
item.content:encoded: 41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights recordLewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.Continue reading...

item.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
item.content:encoded: Kim Yo-jong, sister of Kim Jong-un, issues warning after inspecting border fortifications against backdrop of rising tensionsPropaganda loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be ready to restart within days along the entire border, Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, has said amid a worsening of ties between the two countries.The statement, carried by the state news agency KCNA on Thursday, came a day after she said the loudspeakers would be in operation along the whole border from some time in October.Continue reading...
